Pinned core source resolves sysfs behavior: create_files removes files already created when one sysfs_create_group call fails; on normal unload, platform_device_unregister -> platform_device_del -> device_del -> kobject_del -> sysfs_remove_dir -> kernfs_remove deactivates nodes and drains active references. This establishes normal sysfs teardown ordering, not I/O mapping or OF-node release.

If of_find_compatible_node returns a node, its reference count is incremented. The stock bodies contain no of_node_put, and pinned of_iomap only translates then returns ioremap/ioremap_np; it does not release the node reference. Thus the reference remains unput on that conditional success path.

observations.claim: platform_device_register calls device_initialize then platform_device_add and documents that platform_device_put is required on an error return. The stock init passes static ftm_dev from .data, maps registration errors to -ENODEV, and has no platform_device_put call. The exact stock error branch is established; heap-leak consequences are not inferred.

observations.claim: If platform_device_register succeeds but no device binds, pinned __platform_driver_probe unregisters the driver only and returns -ENODEV. The init failure path frees module memory without calling cleanup_module, while ftm_dev remains the registered static device. This is a conditional stale registered-device pointer/UAF risk; actual branch reachability and runtime fault are unconfirmed.
Normal cleanup unregisters the platform device and sysfs removal drains active kernfs callbacks. That teardown does not unmap the separately stored I/O mappings or put the OF-node reference.

observations.claim: On a sysfs_create_group error, pinned sysfs core rolls back files created by that group. This does not release the module's separately acquired OF reference or I/O mappings.

Stock ftm_dev is a 1008-byte .data object at offset 0; no function relocation lies inside [0,0x3f0), and the first .text relocation is at .data+0x3f8. No dev.release initializer is present. Pinned device_release warns when dev/type/class release is absent and frees device_private, not the containing static object; platform_device_alloc separately installs platform_device_release.

inferences.claim: Conditional on successful OF-node lookup, the reference remains held: the pinned API increments it, of_iomap does not put it, and stock has no of_node_put call. This is a static reference-retention consequence; target runtime lookup success is unknown.

On platform_device_register error, stock omits the API-required platform_device_put. This is a real stock error-path deviation; the available evidence does not establish a heap leak or a runtime fault, so do not claim either.

Conditional on successful platform-device registration followed by no bind, the core leaves the device registered while module init fails and frees module memory without cleanup_module. Because ftm_dev resides in that module image, this is a conditional stale-pointer/UAF risk, not an observed runtime UAF.

Conditional on non-NULL mapping acquisition, stock ftmmod never calls iounmap on either of_iomap's returned mapping or the ioremap_prot mapping. Normal removal only unregisters driver/device, and probe error paths do not unwind them. The pinned source shows of_iomap returns ioremap/ioremap_np and ioremap_prot returns generic_ioremap_prot; these mappings therefore remain unreleased by this module. Target acquisition/unload reachability remains unknown.
